title: Substring XOR Queries
summary: Given a binary string and a series of queries, for each query, find the shortest substring whose decimal value, when XORed with the first number of the query, equals the second number.
statement: Given a binary string and a series of queries, for each query, find the shortest substring whose decimal value, when XORed with the first number of the query, equals the second number. Return the start and end indices of this substring, or [-1, -1] if no such substring exists. If multiple substrings meet the criteria, choose the one starting at the smallest index.
constraints: For each [first,second], seek a binary substring whose value equals first XOR second.
Choose minimum substring length, then minimum starting index.
hints: Each query asks for the fixed target first XOR second.
Precompute the shortest earliest substring for every representable value.
At each start, inspect at most 32 bits because query integers fit that width; stop immediately after a leading zero.
Scanning starts then ends in increasing order makes the first stored representation shortest for a fixed start and earliest among equal lengths.
editorial: Scanning starts then ends in increasing order makes the first stored representation shortest for a fixed start and earliest among equal lengths.

tests.explanation: Targets five and three first appear as shortest substrings at [0,2] and [2,3].
Target four has no binary substring, so the result is [-1,-1].
